# Stride AI Helper Notes

- Monorepo layout: Firebase callable functions in Python at [functions/main.py](functions/main.py); SvelteKit admin dashboard in [stride_admin](stride_admin); Flutter mobile/web apps in [stride_app](stride_app) and [stride_web](stride_web) sharing the Dart package [packages/stride_core](packages/stride_core).
- Data model is Firestore-based and multi-tenant. The canonical schema and role definitions live in [docs/database-design.md](docs/database-design.md); collections include organizations, divisions, users (providers/clients), assignments, admins, and exercises. Keep queries scoped by `organizationId` and align with the documented constraints.
- Python Firebase Functions: callable endpoints like `create_provider`, `update_provider`, `create_client`, `generate_exercise_plan_with_ai`, `get_admins`, etc., are defined in [functions/main.py](functions/main.py) and delegated to helpers under [functions/functions](functions/functions) and [functions/models](functions/models). Every callable passes through `verify_admin`, which checks the caller against the `admins` collection and privilege rules—mirror that pattern for new functions. All functions return `{success, message, ...}` payloads; surface meaningful errors and log via `utils/logger.py`.
- OpenAI usage: `get_openai()` in [functions/main.py](functions/main.py) reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env`; keep prompts and model calls centralized in the exercise helpers and avoid leaking secrets in responses.
- Admin dashboard auth: client login uses Firebase Auth email/password, then exchanges the ID token at [stride_admin/src/routes/v1/auth/session/+server.ts](stride_admin/src/routes/v1/auth/session/+server.ts) to set an HTTP-only `session` cookie. Server hook [stride_admin/src/hooks.server.ts](stride_admin/src/hooks.server.ts) verifies the session via `firebase-admin`, loads the admin doc from Firestore, and guards `(protected)` routes; redirect to `/login` when missing.
- Admin dashboard data access: browser SDK configured in [stride_admin/src/lib/firebase/config.ts](stride_admin/src/lib/firebase/config.ts) (public envs), admin SDK in [stride_admin/src/lib/firebase/admin.ts](stride_admin/src/lib/firebase/admin.ts) (uses `FIREBASE_ADMIN_SDK_KEY`). Client-side services under [stride_admin/src/lib/services](stride_admin/src/lib/services) call callable functions via `httpsCallable` (e.g., [admins.ts](stride_admin/src/lib/services/admins.ts)), converting Firestore timestamps with `toSafeDate`. Server routes under [stride_admin/src/routes/api](stride_admin/src/routes/api) use the admin SDK for direct reads (e.g., divisions GET with optional `organizationId`).
- SvelteKit conventions: uses Svelte 5 runes (`$state`, `$derived`) and Paraglide i18n middleware; follow existing patterns in layout files like [stride_admin/src/routes/(protected)/+layout.svelte](stride_admin/src/routes/(protected)/+layout.svelte). Keep navigation in sync with protected routes and rely on `authStore` for reactive auth state.
- Flutter/Dart shared core: initialize Firebase via [packages/stride_core/lib/services/firebase_config.dart](packages/stride_core/lib/services/firebase_config.dart) before hitting Firestore or Functions. Repositories (e.g., [packages/stride_core/lib/repositories/admin_repo.dart](packages/stride_core/lib/repositories/admin_repo.dart)) wrap callable functions and parse maps into models under `models/*`; new repos should follow the same `_call` + `fromMap` pattern and preserve the `success` contract from the backend.
- Flutter apps: [stride_app](stride_app) and [stride_web](stride_web) depend on `stride_core`; keep app-specific code light and push shared logic into the package to avoid divergence.
- Dev workflows: from repo root, deploy Firebase rules/functions with `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` or `firebase deploy --only functions` (see [README.md](README.md)). Admin dashboard: `cd stride_admin && npm install && npm run dev` (Vite). Flutter apps: run `flutter pub get` then `flutter run` (mobile) or `flutter build web`/`flutter run -d chrome` (web).
- Environment: never commit secrets. Admin dashboard requires the JSON service key in `FIREBASE_ADMIN_SDK_KEY`; public Firebase settings must be set as `PUBLIC_*` vars. Python functions load `.env` for OpenAI.
- Safety/consistency: avoid editing generated Firebase configs (e.g., `firebase_options.dart`). Keep callable names and privilege semantics aligned between frontend services and Python functions. For Firestore reads/writes, include `organizationId`/`divisionId` guards and honor role constraints outlined in the schema doc.

If anything here feels off or incomplete, tell me which sections need more detail and I’ll refine it.
